text:
Sean Gallagher: iterating the rollout checklist for the runtime profile pack. need to lock: (1) canary cohorts (region/model mix) and (2) rollback trigger thresholds. want this to be copy/pastable into the runbook.

Rafael Mendes: +1. right now the checklist is too hand-wavy (“watch p99”). we need explicit gates + who can push the button.

Neha Kapoor: also please include cohort composition that exercises fleet heterogeneity. we have driver spread in hosted in a couple regions.

Allison Grant: if we’re defining gates, we should align with what we can reliably alert on. some metrics are new (kernel_fallback_rate, scheduler_queue_ms tags w/ profile_id). we can gate on latency/error now, and add “watchlist” signals for the rest.

Sean Gallagher: proposal draft:
- Cohort A (Hosted): 1% traffic for 24h, 2 regions, 2 model families
- Cohort B (Hosted): 5% traffic for 24h, 3 regions, broader model set
- Then 25% for 48h, then 100%
Need concrete picks.

Irene Choi: for regions, recommend include:
- us-east-1 (highest volume, most representative)
- eu-west-1 (different host mix)
- ap-southeast-1 (lower volume but tends to show noisy tail)
If we only do 2 in first cohort, do us-east-1 + eu-west-1.

Mateo Alvarez: model mix: we should explicitly include at least one long-context heavy workload (8k+ prompt) + one short chatty workload. kernel fallback issues show up on long ctx.

Sofia Ivanova: scheduler regressions show up under mixed prompt lengths. we should include the “mixed-chat” route (short prompts, medium decodes) AND a “rag-long-prefill” route (long prefill, short decode).

Rafael Mendes: can we define cohort by (region, route group) rather than raw model names? models change more often.

Sean Gallagher: for the checklist we can do both. route group is what SRE can target, but we still need to confirm it hits the model families (llama-ish vs mixtral-ish) + quantized variants.

Allison Grant: from dashboards POV, routing tags we can filter on: region, model_family, profile_id/profile_version, and “workload_bucket” (if scheduler is emitting it). for cohort targeting, easiest is region + route.

Neha Kapoor: don’t forget L40S pools. most of hosted volume is H100 but we need at least a small L40S cohort bc OOM risk is higher there.

Sean Gallagher: ok revised cohorting:
Cohort A (24h):
- H100: us-east-1, routes: mixed-chat + rag-long-prefill
- L40S: us-west-2, route: mixed-chat (smaller), maybe 0.5%?
Cohort B (24h):
- H100: add eu-west-1 + add “batchy-embeddings” route
- L40S: add eu-west-1 (if we have capacity)
Thoughts?

Irene Choi: L40S in eu-west-1 is thin. safer to do L40S in us-west-2 + us-east-1 first.

Rafael Mendes: agree. also, cohort A should include at least one dedicated internal tenant that we control (dogfood) so we can pin/unpin quickly.

Mateo Alvarez: dogfood tenant on H100 in us-east-1 yes. for L40S, dogfood is smaller but ok.

Allison Grant: if we add a “dogfood cohort” we can set stricter alerting since it’s clean traffic.

Sean Gallagher: cool.
Now rollback triggers. I’m thinking “block advancement” vs “rollback immediately”.
Block advancement:
- p95 latency regression > 5% for 30m on any canary cohort (same route)
- error rate (5xx + timeouts) +0.2% absolute for 15m
Rollback immediately:
- p99 latency regression > 10% for 10m OR p99 crosses absolute ceiling (route-specific?)
- OOM / container restart rate > baseline + 2x for 10m
- kernel_fallback_rate > 1% for 15m (H100 only?)

Sofia Ivanova: the p95 gate is fine. but p99 “absolute ceiling” depends heavily on route. can we define it in terms of delta vs baseline with confidence interval? otherwise we’ll false positive.

Allison Grant: we don’t have CI math wired into alerting. simplest is delta vs baseline (previous 7d median p99 for that region/route/model_family) but that baseline query might be heavy.

Rafael Mendes: for checklist v1, keep it simple:
- rollback on sustained p99 delta > X%
- plus error spikes
- plus restart/OOM
Then add kernel fallback as “investigate/rollback if correlated with p99”.

Neha Kapoor: also add “queueing time” signal. when scheduler gets it wrong, scheduler_queue_ms blows up before compute time.

Allison Grant: we can alert on scheduler_queue_ms p95 if we scope to canary cohort. that metric is already in the new dashboard spec.

Sean Gallagher: ok, updated triggers:
Immediate rollback if ANY:
1) p99 latency +15% vs baseline for 10m (cohort scoped)
2) request error rate +0.5% absolute for 10m OR any 5m window > 2x baseline
3) GPU OOM events > 0 (L40S) for 5m sustained OR restart rate 2x baseline for 10m
4) scheduler_queue_ms p95 +25% vs baseline for 10m (cohort scoped)

Block advancement (but not necessarily rollback):
- p95 latency +5% for 30m
- kernel_fallback_rate > 0.5% for 30m (open investigation)

Mateo Alvarez: for L40S, “OOM events > 0” might be too strict if we get a single noisy node. can we say “> 3 OOMs across cohort” or “OOM rate > 0.1% of requests”? depends on how it’s surfaced.

Allison Grant: the signal we have is `runtime_oom_total` counter (tagged by sku + profile_id) and container restarts. we can do “oom_total increase > 2 within 10m” for a cohort.

Rafael Mendes: +1. a single OOM can happen during deploy churn. two+ within 10m is usually real.

Sean Gallagher: adopting: L40S rollback if `runtime_oom_total` increases by >=2 in 10m for canary cohort OR restarts 2x baseline.

Irene Choi: for H100, OOM should basically be zero. so keep H100 stricter (>=1 within 10m).

Sean Gallagher: good call.

Connor O'Brien: release process question: who is allowed to trigger rollback and what exactly is rolled back? profile version? feature flag? both?

Rafael Mendes: both options exist:
- fast kill-switch: disable profile pack (fallback to legacy defaults)
- targeted rollback: pin previous profile_version
Checklist should specify preferred order.

Sean Gallagher: proposing:
Step 1: kill-switch for cohort (feature flag off) if available
Step 2: if issue is profile-specific and kill-switch isn’t enough, pin profile_version to last known good and redeploy
Also add: “announce in #incidents if rollback is triggered”.

Incident Bot: Reminder: if you see customer impact (SLO breach or widespread errors), open an incident and link the canary dashboard. Use /incident create.

Neha Kapoor: please note that B200 cohorts should be “opt-in only” with hard gate; not part of hosted default rollout.

Mateo Alvarez: yep. for runtime-1.22 we’re only defaulting H100/L40S. B200 is explicitly pinned and should have separate checklist.

Allison Grant: I’ll update the dashboard filters for the cohort definitions (region + route + sku + profile_version) and add a saved view for “Canary Cohort A”.

Sofia Ivanova: can we add one more gate: if compute time is flat but queueing time spikes, rollback quicker. that’s the scheduler bug class.

Sean Gallagher: that’s covered by scheduler_queue_ms trigger.

Rafael Mendes: action items:
- Sean: edit checklist doc with cohort A/B definitions + triggers and “who/what/how” rollback steps
- Allison: confirm alert feasibility + saved views
- Irene: sanity check region/SKU availability for L40S cohort
We want this finalized before next go/no-go.

Sean Gallagher: ack. I’ll post updated checklist text here for final review today.

Sean Gallagher: (draft snippet for checklist)
Cohort A (24h):
- H100: us-east-1, dogfood tenant + 1% external, routes: mixed-chat + rag-long-prefill
- L40S: us-west-2, dogfood + 0.5% external, route: mixed-chat
Cohort B (24h):
- H100: add eu-west-1, expand to 5%, add route: batchy-embeddings
- L40S: add us-east-1, expand to 1%
Rollback triggers (cohort scoped):
- H100: p99 +15% vs baseline 10m
- L40S: p99 +15% vs baseline 10m
- errors: +0.5% abs 10m OR 2x baseline 5m
- H100 OOM: runtime_oom_total +1 in 10m
- L40S OOM: runtime_oom_total +2 in 10m
- restarts: 2x baseline 10m
- scheduler_queue_ms p95 +25% vs baseline 10m
Rollback procedure:
1) disable profile pack flag for cohort
2) if persists, pin last known good profile_version
3) if customer impact, /incident create + comms

Allison Grant: looks workable. I’ll confirm the baseline queries are available for p99 deltas; if not, we can temporarily use absolute thresholds per route from the expected behavior doc.

Irene Choi: region/SKU mapping ok for those picks. L40S us-east-1 has enough headroom for 1%.

Connor O'Brien: from release mgmt POV, please add “record profile_version + git sha in release notes and in #eng-releases thread when advancing cohorts”. helps w/ auditing.

Sean Gallagher: will do. thanks all.
